quotes.text: The gap between knowing and acting is exactly where Fabric Data Activator lives, and it's designed to cut that gap down to seconds.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Defines the purpose of Data Activator in one sentence.

quotes.text: When you line it up against the standard BI workflow, the advantage is obvious. Monitoring alone tells you the story. Monitoring plus response changes the outcome
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Crisp contrast between dashboards and automated response.

quotes.text: The root of the problem isn't the lack of detection, it's the lack of intelligence about what to do next.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Names the real cause of alert fatigue.

quotes.text: There's also the temptation to watch everything now. It makes sense at first. More monitored conditions should mean more opportunities to react. But every trigger you defined contributes to the workload running against your fabric capacity.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Warns that triggers consume shared Fabric capacity.

quotes.text: The safer route is to start with high value, low frequency conditions. That means picking scenarios where even if you only trigger a few times a day, each one has a clear impact worth automating.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concrete recommendation for starting with Data Activator.

takeaways: Fabric Data Activator closes the gap between seeing a change in data and acting on it by reacting to event streams in near real time instead of waiting for someone to check a dashboard.
Because it runs next to Power BI, Synapse and Fabric's data warehousing, it can pause pipelines, update records or call external APIs such as CRM, ERP or supplier systems when a condition is met.
Every trigger consumes Fabric capacity and is only as fast as the systems it calls, so start with high-value, low-frequency conditions and plan capacity and latency before scaling.
hook: Most teams call themselves real time, yet their decisions still wait for someone to notice a dashboard or an alert. This episode shows data and operations teams how Fabric Data Activator turns live data streams into automated actions inside and outside Microsoft Fabric, and which capacity and latency limits to plan for.
